skill.name: systematic-debugging
skill.description: Four-phase debugging methodology with root cause analysis. Use when investigating bugs, fixing test failures, or troubleshooting unexpected behavior. Emphasizes NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE FIRST.
skill.summary: Use a four-phase process to diagnose bugs before changing code.

content.user_title: Debug Code with Root Cause Analysis
content.value_statement: Bugs waste time when teams patch symptoms without evidence. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured diagnosis before changes.
actual_capabilities: Guides a four-phase debugging workflow from investigation to implementation.
Emphasizes root cause evidence before applying code changes.
Provides checklists for test failures, runtime errors, regressions, and intermittent failures.
Encourages hypothesis-based testing with one variable changed at a time.
Defines stop conditions when repeated fixes reveal deeper design issues.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts, tools, or automated diagnostics.
Requires access to project logs, stack traces, tests, or reproduction steps.
Does not replace domain expertise for architecture or production incident response.
Cannot guarantee the claimed success rate for every codebase or team.

use_cases.title: Investigate a Failing Test
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to read the full failure, inspect setup, trace bad values, and create a focused fix.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a Runtime Error
use_cases.description: Follow the stack trace, identify invalid state, and add validation where the bad value originates.

use_cases.title: Review Repeated Fix Attempts
use_cases.description: Stop after multiple failed fixes, document findings, and decide whether the design needs team discussion.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Bug Investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the systematic-debugging skill to investigate this bug. First summarize the symptom, reproduction steps, and evidence needed before proposing any fix.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Test Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the systematic-debugging process on this failing test. Read the assertion, inspect setup data, trace the unexpected value, and state the root cause.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Fix Hypothesis
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the hypothesis and testing phase. Form one clear hypothesis, predict the result, choose the smallest test, and explain what each outcome means.

prompt_templates.title: Escalate Repeated Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Use systematic-debugging to review these failed fix attempts. Identify patterns, decide whether to stop patching, and prepare a concise team handoff.

output_examples.input: A unit test fails after a refactor, but the changed function looks correct.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for the full error, compares the old and new call paths, traces the unexpected value, and proposes one testable hypothesis.

output_examples.input: A runtime error appears in production when a field is null.
output_examples.output: The assistant follows the stack trace, identifies where the null value first enters the flow, and recommends validation at that source.

output_examples.input: Three fixes have failed and each exposes a different issue.
output_examples.output: The assistant stops further patching, summarizes evidence, lists suspected design assumptions, and prepares points for team review.

best_practices: Collect reproducible evidence before editing code.
Change one variable at a time when testing a hypothesis.
Document the root cause and verification steps with the final fix.
anti_patterns: Applying a quick patch before understanding why the bug occurs.
Trying several unrelated fixes without a stated hypothesis.
Ignoring repeated failures that suggest a deeper design problem.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants investigate bugs, test failures, runtime errors, and regressions using a structured root cause process.

faq.question: Does it run debugging commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation only. It may guide the assistant to request evidence or suggest normal project checks.

faq.question: Can it fix code directly?
faq.answer: It can guide a fix after the root cause is identified, but it does not contain code patches or scripts.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when a bug is unclear, a test fails, a runtime error appears, or repeated fixes are not working.

faq.question: How does it improve debugging quality?
faq.answer: It separates evidence gathering, pattern comparison, hypothesis testing, and implementation into clear steps.

faq.question: Is it suitable for team workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It encourages documentation, stop conditions, and team discussion when fixes reveal larger design issues.
